title: Proper pro-etale direct image preserves extension-by-zero support
statement:
Let $u:T_1\to T_2$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $j_1:X\hookrightarrow T_1$ and $j_2:X\hookrightarrow T_2$ be quasi-compact open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] satisfying $u\circ j_1=j_2$. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use the constant-ring module sheaves and ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $Ru_*$ and $j_2^*$ be the uncompleted derived direct image and exact inverse image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and let $j_{i!}$ be extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero], applied termwise using its exactness [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]. For every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ put $M=Ru_*j_{1!}K$. The canonical counit of the derived open adjunction [prop-exc-open-adjoint] is an isomorphism:
$$j_{2!}j_2^*M\longrightarrow M.$$
This is a statement of support on the whole pro-etale derived category; it imposes no etale-origin or boundedness condition on $K$.

source.place: Clause (b), compactification independence: agent-extracted proper/open support obligation. Related source: Stacks proetale.tex Tag 09AG, lemma-jshriek-zero (degree-zero specialization vanishing only); this tag does not itself state the derived proper-support assertion.

proof.text: First prove the sheaf-level support assertion. Let $F$ be an $A_X$-module sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Give $T_2\setminus j_2(X)$ its reduced induced closed subscheme $i_2:Z\hookrightarrow T_2$ using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Work over any affine open $O\subset T_2$. By [lem-exc-closed-inverse-image-formula], to show $i_2^*(u_*j_{1!}F)|_{Z\cap O}=0$ it suffices to show $(u_*j_{1!}F)(v(V))=0$ for every affine ind-etale basis object $V$ over $Z\cap O$. Indeed, the inverse image is the sheafification of these values. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-closed-site-functor-properties], $W=v(V)$ is affine over $O$, $W\times_{T_2}Z=V$, and every point of $W$ specializes to a point of $V$. The same formula is valid on underlying abelian sheaves of our constant modules: the scalar action is simply retained under the inverse-image construction of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations].

source.place: Tags 09BK, 09BL (closed-site lift and sheafification formula); setup for 09AG.

proof.text: Put $P=T_1\times_{T_2}W$ and $Z_P=P\times_{T_2}Z$. Every point $t\in P$ specializes to a point of $Z_P$. In fact the image of the closed subset $\overline{\{t\}}\subset P$ under $P\to W$ is closed, since $u$ is universally closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. It contains the image of $t$ and therefore a specialization of that image in $V$; a point of $\overline{\{t\}}$ over that specialization gives the required point of $Z_P$. Properness is preserved by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], so $P$ is quasi-compact and separated over the affine $W$. The complement of $Z_P$ is a quasi-compact open immersion, being the pullback of $j_2$ by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change].

source.place: Tag 09AG setup; universal-closedness specialization argument, written out.

proof.text: Cover $Z_P$ by finitely many affine opens $P_a=\operatorname{Spec}R_a$ of $P$. Write $Z_P\cap P_a=V(I_a)$. Since its complementary open is quasi-compact, a finite principal-open subcover writes $V(I_a)=V(f_{a1},\ldots,f_{as_a})$ with $f_{ab}\in I_a$. By [lem-weil-pbc-wcontractible-closed-localization], $P_a^\sim=\operatorname{Spec}(S_a^{-1}R_a)$, where $S_a$ consists of elements invertible modulo $I_a$, has image exactly the points of $P_a$ specializing to $Z_P\cap P_a$. Every point of $P$ specializes to a point of $Z_P$, hence is in some $P_a$ and in the image of $P_a^\sim$. These finitely many affine ind-Zariski maps are a pro-etale cover of $P$: on an affine open $Q$ of $P$, the intersection $P_a\cap Q$ is affine, since it is the pullback of the closed diagonal of $P\to W$ inside the affine $P_a\times_WQ$. A closed immersion is affine by [def-weil-closed-immersion], and closed immersions pull back by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. The localization pullback to this intersection is affine too, so the inverse images of $Q$ are affine and jointly surjective. The same closed-base-change lemma makes $Z_P$ and its affine restrictions closed subschemes. Stability in [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering] justify the site claim. Viewed over $T_1$, each $P_a^\sim$ is affine weakly etale and all its points specialize to the closed inverse image of $Z$; this follows from the localization description and weakly-etale base-change/composition in that same stability lemma. That closed subscheme is disjoint from $j_1(X)$ because $uj_1=j_2$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-shriek-specialization-zero] gives $(j_{1!}F)(P_a^\sim)=0$. The sheaf equalizer axiom makes $(j_{1!}F)(P)=0$. By the direct-image section formula in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], this is $(u_*j_{1!}F)(W)=0$.

source.place: Tags 096V (closed localization), 09AH (localization covering), 09AG (degree-zero vanishing); finite-cover specialization argument expanded.

proof.text: Steps 1-3 show $i_2^*(u_*j_{1!}F)=0$. The exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], applied on $T_2$ with $M_F=u_*j_{1!}F$, now reads $0\to j_{2!}j_2^*M_F\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}M_F\to0$. Its first arrow is the specified open-adjunction counit, so it is an isomorphism, naturally in every sheaf $F$. Notice that this argument uses neither geometric-stalk conservativity nor a higher-cohomology consequence of Tag 09AG.

Now let $K$ be bounded below. By [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] the module categories on these small sites are Grothendieck abelian with enough injectives, and [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] supplies a bounded-below complex $J^\bullet$ of injective $A_X$-module sheaves representing $K$. Since $j_{1!}$ is exact [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact], $j_{1!}J^\bullet$ represents $j_{1!}K$. Apply [lem-sp-proetale-open-injective-proper-acyclic] to the square with $C=E=X$, $r=1_X$, $B=T_1$, $D=T_2$, $k=j_1$, $i=j_2$, $p=u$; identity is proper directly from its defining conditions. All open immersions are quasi-compact by hypothesis. Every term $j_{1!}J^a$ is $u_*$-acyclic. The bounded-below complexes clause of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] consequently computes $M=Ru_*j_{1!}K$ by $u_*j_{1!}J^\bullet$. Step 4 makes the actual counit an isomorphism in every degree of this representing complex. Its localization is therefore exactly the derived counit $j_{2!}j_2^*M\to M$ of [prop-exc-open-adjoint], and is an isomorphism.

source.place: Agent derived-resolution argument following the pattern of more-etale.tex Tag 0F7B; the pro-etale acyclicity is separately named, not supplied by that tag.

proof.text: Here is the elementary sheaf-product argument, replacing a separate product lemma. For a quasi-compact open $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, choose its reduced closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Put $P=\prod_a j_!F_a$ for a countable family of constant-$A$ module sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] and preservation of products by both immersion inverse images [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation], we have $i^*P=\prod_a i^*j_!F_a=0$ and $j^*P=\prod_a j^*j_!F_a\cong\prod_aF_a$. The same open-closed sequence therefore makes the counit $j_!j^*P\to P$ an isomorphism. Under the displayed identification its composite with each projection $P\to j_!F_a$ is $j_!$ of the corresponding projection, by naturality of the counit and the open unit $j^*j_!\cong1$. Thus it is precisely the canonical product comparison $j_!(\prod_aF_a)\to\prod_a j_!F_a$. This applies to $j=j_1$ and uses identified constant coefficient rings throughout.

source.place: Tag 09BP, lemma-j-shriek-limits, deduced here in a few lines from the existing ringed open-closed and immersion-limit statements; no new node.

proof.text: Countable products in pro-etale module categories are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. By [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective], products of K-injective representatives represent derived products. Termwise products of arbitrary representing complexes also represent derived products: resolve each factor by a K-injective, take the product of the quasi-isomorphisms, and use exactness of products to see that its cone, the product of the acyclic cones, is acyclic. Thus an exact functor preserving countable sheaf products preserves countable derived products. Apply this to $j_{1!}$ using its product preservation proved in step 6 and [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]. Also apply it to $i_2^*$: [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation] states both its exactness and its preservation of all sheaf limits for identified coefficient rings. Here the coefficients are constant $A$, with their canonical inverse-image identification. These exact functors induce triangulated functors by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated].

source.place: Tag 09BP and exact products; explicit passage from sheaf products to derived products.

proof.text: The functor $Ru_*$ is triangulated and right adjoint to exact inverse image by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Hence it preserves countable derived products by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits]. Together with step 7, this says that $F=Ru_*j_{1!}$ and $i_2^*F$ are triangulated and preserve countable products. Recall [def-weil-derived-limit]: a tower $(N_n,t_n)$ has a homotopy-limit triangle $L\to\prod_nN_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nN_n\to L[1]$, where $\operatorname{pr}_ns=t_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$. Applying $F$ preserves this triangle and, under its canonical product comparisons, preserves precisely $1-s$, since it preserves each projection and each transition. The same holds for $i_2^*$. We use only this triangle property; no uniqueness of a third arrow between triangles or of an arbitrary triangulated homotopy-limit comparison is assumed.

source.place: Right-adjoint product preservation and the defining Roos fibre triangle.

proof.text: For arbitrary $K$, put $K_n=\tau_{\geq-n}K$. Every pro-etale object has a cover by affine weakly contractible objects by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-wcontractible-covering-family]. On such an object evaluation is exact: a section of the target of a module epimorphism has locally a lift, the corresponding epimorphism of sheaves of lifts has a section by weak contractibility, and left exactness is the sheaf equalizer property. Hence $H^p(W,F)=0$ for $p>0$ and every module sheaf $F$, by applying the exact evaluation to an injective resolution. Apply [lem-kun-site-truncation-derived-limit] with this covering family and $d=0$. Its hypotheses hold for every negative cohomology sheaf of $K$, and it gives the triangle $K\to\prod_nK_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nK_n\to K[1]$. Thus the required lower-truncation homotopy limit is $K$ itself, with its canonical truncation maps.

source.place: Tag 0D6P, lemma-is-limit-dimension, with the locally weakly-contractible basis of proetale.tex and d=0.

proof.text: For each $K_n$, step 5 gives $j_{2!}j_2^*F(K_n)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(K_n)$. The exact sheaf sequence in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] yields, on any representing complex $C$, a short exact sequence of complexes $0\to j_{2!}j_2^*C\to C\to i_{2*}i_2^*C\to0$. The closed counit $i_2^*i_{2*}\cong\operatorname{id}$ and $i_2^*j_{2!}=0$ are also in that cited statement. It follows that $i_2^*F(K_n)=0$. Apply $i_2^*F$ to the truncation triangle of step 9. By step 8 its two product terms are products of these zero objects. The resulting triangle has the form $i_2^*F(K)\to0\to0\to i_2^*F(K)[1]$, whence $i_2^*F(K)=0$ by the exact Hom sequence. In the short exact sequence of complexes just displayed for a representative $C$ of $F(K)$, $i_2^*C$ is therefore acyclic. Exactness of $i_{2*}$, again stated by the cited ringed open-closed lemma, makes $i_{2*}i_2^*C$ acyclic. Thus its first arrow is a quasi-isomorphism. That arrow is termwise the specified open counit, so its localization is exactly $j_{2!}j_2^*Ru_*j_{1!}K\to Ru_*j_{1!}K$, as required. This identifies the actual counit, without using a possibly noncanonical isomorphism between homotopy limits.

source.place: Conclusion of the agent proof: product/fibre argument for the specified natural counit.
